metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Trust Model
metadata.description: Formal trust model defining actor trust levels and identifying trust boundary edges where data flows between actors of different trust levels.

actors.name: End User
actors.rationale: External entity providing arbitrary inputs. All user-supplied data (amounts, proofs, addresses) must be validated before processing. Users may attempt malicious actions such as double-spending, invalid proofs, or overflow attacks.

actors.name: zERC20 Token Contract
actors.rationale: Core on-chain smart contract under audit. Enforces value constraints (<=2^248-1) and maintains authoritative hash chain state. Part of the trusted computing base.

actors.name: Verifier Contract
actors.rationale: Core security-critical on-chain contract under audit. Validates zkSNARK proofs, enforces monotonicity for double-spend prevention, and coordinates cross-chain messaging. Part of the trusted computing base.

actors.name: Hub Contract
actors.rationale: Core on-chain contract under audit. Central aggregation point for transfer roots. Computes Poseidon aggregation trees and broadcasts global roots. Part of the trusted computing base.

actors.name: LiquidityManager Contract
actors.rationale: Core on-chain contract under audit. Sole authority for minting/burning zERC20 tokens. Implements incentive curves and anchors supply to reserves. Part of the trusted computing base.

actors.name: Adaptor Contract
actors.rationale: Core on-chain contract under audit. Coordinates cross-chain exits via Stargate bridge. Enforces slippage limits and refund mechanisms. Part of the trusted computing base.

actors.name: Indexer Service
actors.rationale: Off-chain service that indexes events and generates Merkle proofs. While it follows protocol, its outputs (Merkle proofs) must be independently verifiable on-chain. Data integrity depends on correct indexing of blockchain events.

actors.name: Decider/Prover Service
actors.rationale: Off-chain service converting Nova IVC proofs to Groth16 proofs. While computationally trusted to perform correct transformations, its outputs are cryptographically verified on-chain. A malicious prover cannot forge valid proofs.

actors.name: LayerZero v2 Network
actors.rationale: External cross-chain messaging infrastructure. Trusted to deliver messages reliably between chains with supermajority guardian signing. However, message contents must still be validated by receiving contracts.

actors.name: Stargate Bridge
actors.rationale: External cross-chain liquidity bridge. Trusted for asset transfers but subject to bridge-specific risks. Slippage limits provide user protection against unexpected value loss.

actors.name: IC Key Manager Canister
actors.rationale: Internet Computer canister for stealth address secret management. External infrastructure with its own security model. Secrets derived from VetKey are used client-side for privacy operations.

actors.name: IC Storage Canister
actors.rationale: Internet Computer canister for encrypted state storage. External infrastructure providing data persistence. Encryption (AES-GCM) ensures data confidentiality even if storage is compromised.

actors.name: Poseidon Hash Circuit
actors.rationale: Cryptographic primitive implementation using light-poseidon library. Core component of ZK circuits. Correctness is essential for proof security and must match on-chain verification.

actors.name: Baby JubJub Curve Operations
actors.rationale: Cryptographic primitive for elliptic curve operations within ZK circuits. Core component ensuring stealth address derivation correctness. Part of the trusted cryptographic base.

actors.name: Nova Folding Circuit
actors.rationale: Core ZK circuit implementation using sonobe/folding-schemes. Generates IVC proofs for efficient aggregation. Correctness is cryptographically enforced through proof verification.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where untrusted user input enters the trusted LiquidityManager contract to initiate a wrap operation.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The LiquidityManager must validate all wrap request parameters including amount bounds, sender balance, and ensure the underlying token transfer succeeds before minting zERC20.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where trusted system state (wrap completion) transitions to untrusted user possession of tokens.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Token transfer to user is authorized only after successful wrap completion. No additional validation required as this is an outbound flow.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where untrusted user requests unwrap operation from trusted LiquidityManager.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The LiquidityManager must validate unwrap amount against user's zERC20 balance, ensure sufficient underlying liquidity exists, and calculate fees correctly before burning tokens.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where untrusted user initiates token transfer to zERC20 contract.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The zERC20 contract must validate transfer value <= 2^248-1, verify sender has sufficient balance, and update hash chain atomically with balance changes.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where untrusted user begins private transfer flow by generating stealth address.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: N/A - same trust level. Stealth address generation is client-side with no trust boundary crossing.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where untrusted user submits Nova IVC proof to semi-trusted prover service.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The Prover service must deserialize and locally verify the IVC proof before conversion. Invalid proofs should be rejected. The prover cannot forge valid Groth16 proofs from invalid inputs.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where semi-trusted prover service returns Groth16 proof to untrusted user.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Proof delivery to user requires no additional validation. The cryptographic soundness of Groth16 ensures users cannot exploit malformed proofs on-chain.

boundary_edges.description: Critical trust boundary where untrusted user submits teleport request with Groth16 proof to trusted Verifier.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The Verifier must: (1) validate root reference against provedTransferRoots or globalTransferRoots, (2) verify recipient hash binding, (3) enforce strictly increasing totalTeleported for double-spend prevention, (4) cryptographically verify the Groth16 proof before minting any tokens.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where untrusted user initiates cross-chain exit via trusted Adaptor.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The Adaptor must validate user's zERC20 balance before unwrapping and ensure slippage limits protect against sandwich attacks during bridging.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where semi-trusted LayerZero network delivers transfer root message to trusted Hub.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The Hub must validate the sender EID matches a registered Verifier before updating transferRoots. LayerZero's supermajority guardian signing provides message authenticity but the Hub must still verify authorization.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where semi-trusted LayerZero network delivers global root broadcast to trusted Verifier.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The Verifier must validate the message originates from the authorized Hub contract before storing global roots. Invalid sender EIDs must be rejected.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where trusted Verifier sends transfer root to semi-trusted LayerZero for cross-chain delivery.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Message submission to LayerZero is authorized only after successful proof validation. LayerZero must reliably deliver the message; delivery failures require retry mechanisms.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where trusted Hub broadcasts aggregation root via semi-trusted LayerZero to all Verifiers.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Broadcast is authorized only after successful aggregation computation. LayerZero must deliver to all registered Verifiers; partial delivery creates inconsistent global state.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where trusted Adaptor sends assets via semi-trusted Stargate bridge.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Slippage limits in bridge parameters protect user value. Stargate must complete the transfer or trigger refund mechanisms. Bridge failures must not result in lost funds.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where trusted zERC20 contract emits events consumed by semi-trusted Indexer.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Events emitted by zERC20 are authoritative. The Indexer must correctly parse and index all events without omission. Merkle proofs generated from indexed data are independently verifiable on-chain.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary in sub-graph GRAPH-NOVA-PROOF-GENERATION where untrusted user fetches Merkle proofs from semi-trusted Indexer.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Merkle proofs from Indexer are inputs to client-side ZK proof generation. Invalid proofs will cause proof generation to fail or produce invalid proofs rejected on-chain. No trust escalation risk.

boundary_edges.description: Trust boundary where untrusted user submits Nova proof to trusted Verifier for transfer root validation.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The Verifier must cryptographically verify the proof via IRootDecider.verifyOpaqueNovaProof() before storing the transfer root. Invalid proofs must be rejected. Divergent proofs for the same index must trigger emergency state.

critical_security_boundaries.rationale: Primary attack surface for double-spend and invalid proof attacks. Untrusted user submits withdrawal proof that if validated incorrectly could mint unauthorized tokens.
Transfer root proof submission. Invalid proofs could poison the provedTransferRoots mapping enabling future invalid withdrawals.
Entry point for value into the system. Must ensure underlying tokens are received before minting zERC20 to prevent inflation attacks.
Exit point for value from the system. Must ensure zERC20 is burned before releasing underlying to prevent double-withdrawal.
Cross-chain root aggregation. A spoofed message could inject invalid transfer roots affecting cross-chain teleports.
Global root reception enables cross-chain withdrawals. A spoofed global root could enable unauthorized cross-chain minting.
